message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – A Quick Reference Guide** | Topic | Key Points | Where to Find More Info | |-------|------------|------------------------| | **Speed Limits** | • General limit: 55 mph on rural roads, 45 mph on urban roads.
• 70 mph on interstate highways (except where posted otherwise).
• 65 mph on freeways in urban areas. | Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT) – Speed Limit Guidelines | | **Seat‑belt & Child‑Safety** | • All occupants must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster.
• No “seat‑belt law” for drivers over 18, but all passengers must buckle. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Cell‑Phone Use** | • Hand‑held phone use while driving is illegal.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed.
• Texting while driving is prohibited. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) of 0.08% or higher is illegal.
• Zero‑tolerance for drivers under 21 (0.02% BAC).
• Penalties include fines, license suspension, and possible jail time. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • Yield to pedestrians at crosswalks.
• Stop at red lights and stop signs.
• “Yield” signs require slowing and yielding to traffic. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **School Bus** | • Stop for a school bus with its stop sign extended and lights flashing.
• Cannot pass a stopped school bus until it resumes motion. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Lane‑Changing & Overtaking** | • Must signal 100 ft before changing lanes.
• Overtaking on the right is prohibited unless the vehicle ahead is turning left. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Headlights & Lighting** | • Headlights must be on from sunset to sunrise, and during rain, fog, or low visibility.
• Fog lights may be used only when visibility is less than 200 ft. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Towing & Tow‑away** | • Towing a vehicle requires a valid towing permit.
• Tow‑away of a vehicle on a public road requires a police officer’s authorization. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Parking** | • No parking in front of a driveway, fire hydrant, or within 20 ft of a crosswalk.
• Parking on a sidewalk is prohibited. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Vehicle Registration & Inspection** | • Vehicles must be registered and display a valid license plate.
• Most vehicles must pass an annual safety inspection. | Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) | | **Insurance** | • Minimum liability coverage: $30,000 for bodily injury per person, $60,000 for bodily injury per accident, $25,000 for property damage. | Texas Insurance Code | | **Special Situations** | • **High‑way Speed‑Limit**: 70 mph on interstates (except where posted).
• **Construction Zones**: Follow posted signs; speed limits may be reduced.
• **Emergency Vehicles**: Yield to emergency vehicles with lights or sirens. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | --- ### How to Stay Updated 1. **Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT)** – Official website: [https://www.txdot.gov](https://www.txdot.gov) 2. **Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV)** – Official website: [https://www.txdmv.gov](https://www.txdmv.gov) 3. **Texas Legislature Online** – Search for the Texas Transportation Code: [https://capitol.texas.gov](https://capitol.texas.gov) 4. **Local County Courts** – For specific local ordinances or recent changes. --- ### Quick Tips for Safe Driving in Texas - **Always keep your headlights on** during low‑visibility conditions. - **Use hands‑free devices** if you need to talk on the phone. - **Check your speed limit signs**—they can change frequently, especially near construction zones. - **Keep a safe following distance** (at least 2–3 seconds behind the vehicle in front). - **Never drive under the influence**—the penalties are severe and the risk is high. Feel free to ask if you need details on a specific law, recent changes, or how to handle a particular driving scenario!
